references.text: Luke's own account of how the chief priests and council members brought Jesus to Pilate to have him condemned – a direct fulfillment of what the disciples refer to in [ref:Luk 23:1|Luke 23:1].

Pilate declared Jesus innocent, but the chief priests and leaders of the people demanded that he be crucified, and Pilate handed Jesus over to their will ([ref:Luk 23:13-25|Luke 23:13-25]). This is the background for the expression "handed him over to be condemned and crucified".
Jesus himself predicted that he would be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, condemned to death, and delivered to the Gentiles to be crucified ([ref:Matt 20:18-19|Matthew 20:18-19]).
Matthew's parallel account of how the chief priests and elders of the people made the decision to take Jesus' life and handed him over to Pilate ([ref:Matt 27:1-2|Matthew 27:1-2]).
Jesus predicted that the Son of Man would be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, condemned to death, and crucified ([ref:Mark 10:33-34|Mark 10:33-34]).
Mark tells us that the chief priests, along with the elders and the whole council, bound Jesus, led him away, and handed him over to Pilate ([ref:Mark 15:1|Mark 15:1]).
In John's Gospel, the chief priests and servants cry out "Crucify! Crucify!" ([ref:Joh 19:6|John 19:6]), showing the active role of the chief priests in demanding Jesus' crucifixion.
John tells us that Pilate handed Jesus over to them to be crucified, and they took him, led him out, and crucified him ([ref:Joh 19:16-18|John 19:16-18]).

Peter proclaims on the day of Pentecost that Jesus was handed over according to God's set plan and foreknowledge, and that they nailed him to the cross and killed him by the hands of lawless men ([ref:Apg 2:23|Acts 2:23]).
Peter accuses Israel's leaders of having handed Jesus over and denied him before Pilate, and of killing the author of life ([ref:Apg 3:13-15|Acts 3:13-15]).
Peter declares to the council members and chief priests that Jesus Christ from Nazareth, whom they crucified, has been raised by God from the dead ([ref:Apg 4:10|Acts 4:10]).

Paul proclaims that the inhabitants of Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize Jesus, but fulfilled the words of the prophets by condemning him and asking Pilate to have him put to death ([ref:Apg 13:27-28|Acts 13:27-28]).
